lines.text: Vera, do we know how a model works?
We see every multiplication. Not why they add up to behaviour.
Who works that out?
Interpretability. It matters for safety, debugging and trust.
Where do you even start?
The logit lens: stop partway up and ask for an answer now.
Low down: “the”. Up top: “Paris”. Illustrative numbers.
lines.say: Low down: the. Up top: Paris. Illustrative numbers.

lines.text: The guess sharpens as it climbs.
Why not read each neuron?
More concepts than dimensions, packed at almost-perpendicular angles.
lines.say: More concepts than dimensions, packed at almost perpendicular angles.

lines.text: They're rarely active together, so it works. When two are, they leak.
Cat and code on, and Paris lights up!
So how do you pull them apart?
Sparse autoencoders unpack them into millions of cleaner features.
lines.say: Sparse auto-encoders unpack them into millions of cleaner features.

lines.text: Anthropic found one for the Golden Gate Bridge.
Can you turn it up?
Push along it: Golden Gate Claude brought every chat back to the bridge.
Real maths, made-up base numbers.
But does a feature cause the answer?
Paste one activation from a clean run into a corrupted one.
Second John, layer 3: 83% back. That spot carries it.
lines.say: Second John, layer three: eighty-three percent back. That spot carries it.

lines.text: Why not just ask the model?
That's generated text. Anthropic caught a model doing sums one way, describing another.
So judge it by what it does.
Behaviour and evals. It's young science: insight on about a quarter of prompts.
Can I look inside too?
Try the logit lens and the steering dial in the Inside the box chapter.
Strength nine. I'm a bridge now.
